No reference to the four rules? You mentioned some of the content, but it's usually better to specify they are the four rules of firearm safety.

Treat all guns as if they are loaded.

Never let the muzzle cover anything you are not willing to destroy.

Keep your finger off the trigger until your sights are on the target.

Be sure of your target and what is beyond it. These should always be reinforced.

Everyone should be familiar with the four rules.

Another point, not all guns have a manual safety, and you should never rely on a safety to be safe with a gun. An AR-15 is a VERY practical solution for this. It is very easy to learn to shoot accurately, has a generous magazine capacity, relatively low recoil, and doesn't over-penetrate as much as other options. If things get really bad, you'll also be more likely to be able to find more ammo and parts for one. The AR-15 platform is VERY modular, and you can find a build that will meet most needs.

"But shouldn't I get a handgun?" That depends. Handguns are a thing because they are smaller and easier to carry. That's really the only real reason for a handgun. If you're not going to carry a gun outside the house, and want to just be able to hole up in a corner with a gun pointed at the door, then you probably don't need a handgun. A handgun can be very useful to carry around your home, and you can generally carry a handgun within your own home without restrictions.
